evidence.curator_note: Same drawn scheme as IMS8-EQ8.58a, instantiated for the SECOND printed substituent set (R = CH3), i.e. 2,2,4,4-tetramethylcyclobutanone. Book draws 2 arc(s) on the first (leftmost) structure; moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn arc 1 = a fishhook from the odd electron of the n-ionized oxygen (the printed '+.' sits on O, the C=O double bond drawn intact) into the C(1)-O(2) bond; drawn arc 2 = a fishhook from the ring C(1)-C(3) sigma bond into that same C-O bond, raising it from double to triple (acylium). The undrawn move 3 puts the second electron of the cleaved C(1)-C(3) bond on C(3), which the book shows only as a radical dot in the next structure. The carbonyl carbon is in the ring, so this alpha cleavage merely OPENS the ring with no mass loss. Map numbers: 1 = carbonyl C, 2 = O, 3 = the alpha carbon cleaved off C1 (left CR2 of the diamond), 4 = the CH2 at the bottom of the diamond, 5 = the alpha carbon retained by the acyl group (right CR2); 6,7 = the two methyls on C3 and 8,9 = the two methyls on C5.

Book draws 2 arc(s) on the second (ring-opened) structure; moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). Drawn arc 1 = a fishhook from the radical dot on C(3) into the forming C(3)=C(4) pi bond; drawn arc 2 = a fishhook from the C(4)-C(5) sigma bond into that same forming pi bond. The undrawn move 3 puts the second electron of C(4)-C(5) on C(5) - printed by the book as the dot next to the product's 'R2'. Both arrows on the page carry the label 'alpha'. For R = CH3 the expelled olefin is 2-methylpropene, C4H8 (m/z 56, not printed), and the charge stays on the C4H6O acyl fragment.

Book draws 0 arc(s) here: it prints a double-headed resonance arrow linking the drawn product .R2C-C(triple bond)O+ with the ionized-ketene form R2C=C=O(+.) ('+.' on the oxygen, the two R groups on the terminal carbon). All three encoded moves are curator-supplied bookkeeping for that resonance interconversion. Convention (C): the fragmentation steps are written to the LOCALIZED acylium/alkyl-radical form drawn first and this step converts it to the ketene form drawn second; they are one ion, so only the ketene form is flagged detected. The text above the scheme motivates exactly this stabilization, quoting IE(Me2C=C=O) ~ 8.4 eV.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for equation 8.58 - no MOD Rule.fromDFS encodes this cyclobutanone double-alpha-cleavage, so no cross-link is asserted. The nearest indexed generic carbonyl alpha-cleavage rule, IMS_4_14 (DFS '[C]1([C]2[C]3)([C]4[C]5){=}[O+.]>>[C.]2[C]3.[C]4[C]5[C]1{#}[O+]'), was CHECKED and is NOT a valid stand-in: loading it in MOD yields left edges (C1-C2, C1-C4, C1=O) and right edges (C1-C5, C1#O), so it breaks BOTH bonds at the carbonyl carbon and re-bonds the acylium to C5 (the terminal carbon of the retained chain) instead of C4 - a skeletal rearrangement that also over-fills C5's valence. Its left pattern does match 2,2,4,4-tetramethylcyclobutanone (RDKit SMARTS [#6](-[#6]-[#6])(-[#6]-[#6])=[O+], 8 matches, the second carbon of each branch being a methyl), so on this substrate the rule would FIRE and emit a rearranged, valence-invalid product; it fails outright (0 matches) on the R = H case of IMS8-EQ8.58a. Recorded as a rule mismatch, not a cross-link. ms_context: the page prints no electron energy; the scheme belongs to ordinary EI-spectrum discussion (Figure 8.4 on the same page is an EI mass spectrum, book standard 70 eV), so EI/70 eV/[M]+. is used. precursor_mz 126.1039 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of the 2,2,4,4-tetramethylcyclobutanone molecular ion for the printed R = CH3 instantiation, not a number printed on the page.

The page prints, directly under the scheme, 'R = CH3 : m/z 70, 100%'. relative_intensity 1.0 is that printed base-peak percentage; observed_mz 70.0413 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of the C4H6O(+.) dimethylketene radical cation, consistent with the printed nominal 70.
